examples.condition: An exact UPRN point identifies an addressable location but does not prove broadband availability.
Nearest-UPRN assignment is prohibited; an exact current UPRN relation and release receipt are required.
OS Open UPRN includes non-postal features, so a UPRN must not be silently typed as a home or business.
Six-week UPRN and linked-identifier updates require pinned versions and must not silently overwrite prior joins.
A UPRN-USRN-TOID link supports identifier reconciliation but is not an exact registered-title extent.
NSUL and ONSUD geography products cannot supply or upgrade broadband metrics.
ONSUD point-in-polygon allocates a UPRN to geography and must not be treated as a parcel-boundary test.
ONS postcode attribution is corroborative only because ONS reports no formal postcode-inclusion agreement.
HMLR INSPIRE is freehold-only; absence of a polygon cannot be interpreted as absence of a premises.
A polygon duplicated across local-authority files must be deduplicated by exact Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
An INSPIRE polygon shows indicative extent and cannot establish the exact land in a registered title.
One registered title may contain several separate polygons, so one polygon is not automatically one premises.
A BNG-to-WGS84 shift of up to 15 metres prevents exact-nearest promotion without transformation receipts.
BDUK UPRN data separates current connectivity, future commercial plans and intervention plans; those states must not be collapsed.
White, Grey and Black classifications can include current or planned infrastructure over a three-year horizon.
Under Review is fail-closed because current claims may be unverified or planned delivery may retain evidence gaps.
